title: Hearty Slow Vietnamese Lentils Banh Mi
description: A romantic and shattering Vietnamese dish featuring slow-cooked lentils in a banh mi, perfect for a Buddhist temple gathering, this fermented lentil banh mi is a hearty twist on traditional Vietnamese street food.
instructions: In a large pot, combine the lentils and vegetable broth, and bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for 30 minutes, or until the lentils are tender.
While the lentils are cooking, toast the baguette by baking it in a preheated oven at 350 degrees for 10 minutes.
Spread the sriracha mayo on the toasted baguette.
Assemble the banh mi by spooning the cooked lentils onto the baguette, followed by the pickled carrots, pickled daikon, cucumber, and cilantro.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Note: this recipe is for refrigerator pickling/preserving only — store in the refrigerator and consume within 1 week. Do not water-bath can without an acid (vinegar or lemon juice).
